cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This door's lock will need replacing. Nobody touches it until I've checked the mechanism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. I tighten it every week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we begin with the hinge. Don't skip straight to tightening; show me which part moves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The screw spins in its hole. We'll need a longer one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Longer isn't a specification. Show me the replacement you would choose so I can approve it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 announces lock replacement but B2 identifies the hinge. A3 claims the new starting point and corrects rushed tightening; A5 uses B4's proposed length to make B choose under A's approval.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies the actual component, and B4 supplies observed screw behavior and remedy. Each answer gives A a new instruction to issue while preserving authority.

relationship.evidence: B2 routinely tightens the hinge and B4 notices the spinning screw, so B is the knowledgeable participant A pretends to supervise.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4's useful solution an insufficient specification, extending A's sole-approval pose through dependence on B's choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 door failure, B2 hinge and B4 spinning screw make the practical sequence legible without hidden repair history.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's specification correction has an immediate task: B must pick a replacement. The final conditional wording avoids inventing previous replacement use.
